## Part B - Data Frames and Conditional Statement

##B1
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

print(students)
```

##B2
```{r}
str(students)

dim(students)

colnames(students)

summary(students)
```

##B3
```{r}
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)

print(students)
```

##B4
```{r}
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75

print(students)
```

##B5
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(
  students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support")
)

print(students)
```

##B6
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

result <- sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
print(result)
```

## Part C - Rbind() And Cbind()

##C1
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(
  new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support")
)


students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
print(students_all)
```

##C2
```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)

class(students_all)
```

##C3
```{r}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)

m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))

print(m)
```

##C4
```{r}
# rbind() requires every data frame you pass it to have the exact same column names. If any column names differ, the function stops and throws the error Error in rbind(deparse.level, ...) : names do not match previous names. Wrapping the rbind() call in tryCatch() intercepts this error, uses message() to print the issue clearly, and returns NULL so your script can keep running instead of crashing.

bad <- data.frame(score1 = 80, score2 = 85)

result <- tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad), 
  error = function(e) { 
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL 
  }
)
```

## Part D - Subsetting

##D1
```{r}
students_all$name

students_all[["name"]]

students_all[, "name"]
```

##D2
```{r}
students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```

##D3
```{r}
students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
```

##D4
```{r}
subset(
  students_all, 
  sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75, 
  select = c(name, section, final)
)
```

##D5
```{r}
highest_student <- students_all$name[which.max(students_all$average)]
print(highest_student)

lowest_student <- students_all$name[which.min(students_all$average)]
print(lowest_student)
```

##D6
```{r}
sorted_students <- students_all[order(-students_all$average), ]

head(sorted_students, 3)
```

## Part E - Basic Factors

##E1
```{r}
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
```

##E2
```{r}
table(students_all$sex)

table(students_all$section)

table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)
```

##E3
```{r}
as.integer(students_all$sex)

#factors are saved as numbers behind the scenes, linked to a separate list of text labels. Because R sorts these labels alphabetically ("F" before "M"), it uses the number 1 to represent "F" and the number 2 to represent "M".
```

##E4
```{r}
students_all$sex_label <- factor(
  students_all$sex, 
  levels = c("F", "M"), 
  labels = c("Female", "Male")
)

levels(students_all$sex_label)
```

##E5
```{r}
summary(students_all$sex_label)

mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])

mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])
```
